description: Cellular and compartmentalised. Living bright bedrooms dim. Deep — views through multiple spaces. Clear functional corridor connecting zones. Kitchen: L-shaped or U-shaped, no island or peninsula — counter set back from windows, moderate natural light. Cook faces the wall — back to the living and dining area. Two cooks can work simultaneously on separate counter runs. Fully open plan — no wall separates kitchen from dining and living. Living arrangement: split seating-kitchen-dining, kitchen on side wall. Seating: Sofa in the living area near the upper exterior windows facing the TV wall; dining table with four chairs set centrally near the kitchen.. Dining table (4 seats). TV on wall opposite wall to entry. Cook cannot see TV from cooking position. Diners do not face the TV. Entry: corridor entry, first thing visible on arrival is bedroom doors, L-shaped corridor, medium length. No door between entry and living — relevant where local regulations require separation. Double bedroom — accessed via own door off corridor, no walk-in wardrobe. Double bedroom closest to entry — lighter acoustic separation from the arrival zone. Secondary bedroom 1 — accessed via own door off corridor, desk visible, 14 m² — large enough for bunk beds. Secondary bedroom 2 — accessed via own door off corridor, desk visible, 14 m² — large enough for bunk beds. Each single bedroom can function as a dedicated home office, hobby room, guest room, or children's bedroom. 2 of 2 have a desk visible in plan. Single bedroom use options: children's bedroom / dedicated home office / hobby or creative studio / guest room / home office + children's bedroom simultaneously / bunk bed setup in the larger room — two children sharing, other bedroom freed as dedicated office or hobby space. Storage: generous wardrobe storage. Sanitary rooms: bathroom (shower and toilet); bathroom (shower, bathtub, and toilet). Two bathrooms — two people can shower simultaneously, parallel morning and evening routines possible. Suits: families with two or more children; multi-generational households; families wanting two children sharing one large bedroom (bunk beds), keeping the other bedroom as a dedicated office or hobby space. Not suitable for: wheelchair users needing step-free wide circulation (narrow compartmentalised corridors and multiple doors); those wanting a master ensuite (bathrooms accessed off corridor, not from bedrooms); people wanting a large open social living space (living zone is split and broken up by walls).
